To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Communication apprehensiveness can be measured and is predictive of participation in an on-line environment.

communication apprehensiveness is negatively correlated with on-line learning performance and that the relationship between apprehension and performance is stronger for individuals who have the opportunity to select their learning venue.

communication apprehensive students are less likely than nonapprehensive students to participate in on-line learning environments, that communication apprehensive participants are less likely to choose to participate in on-online learning environments, and that communication apprehensive learners are less likely to achieve higher grades than nonapprehensives.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of on-line learning environments that provide the individual with the ability to participate in a manner that is consistent with his or her communication predispositions.
the use of web and other on-line technologies to enhance the learning experience of students in higher education.
the design of on-line environments that are sensitive to the individual's communication predisposition, and how that predisposition affects learning performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the on-line environment is not a panacea for all learning problems.
the on-line learning experience is not a panacea for all learners and the design of on-line environments should take into consideration the individual learner's predispositions.

the use of on-line learning environments can provide enhanced learning experiences to individuals who are predisposed to participate within these environments, while the learning experience for those who are not predisposed may be negatively impacted.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of computer-mediated learning environments may provide a means of re-engineering participation in the higher education classroom.
we have found that communication apprehension can be a significant factor in determining the success of a learner's participation within an on-line environment.
on-line learning environments can be designed with a focus upon individual learners, but only to the extent that the learner's predispositions toward communication activities are taken into account.
The main takeaway from our work is that
on-line learning environments can be designed to enhance the learning experience of all students, regardless of their predisposition to participate in on-line communication venues.
the on-line environment is a powerful learning medium that can be used to enhance the learning experience.
the design and implementation of on-line learning tools should take into account an individuals' predisposition to engage with the communication medium.
